svg.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Two clocks
svg.desc: Schematic timeline from 24 months before launch to 6 months after. Top, the demand clock: a declaration's open size range narrows in steps at decision events (funding approval, design review, go/no-go; a named owner and a completed ramp are marked hollow, as evidence rather than events), from Intent (months −18 to −9) to Dated (−9 to −3), Configured (−3 to launch), Live (launch to +3) and Organic (after ramp). Bottom, the supply clock: five layers, each a bar ending at launch whose left end is its commit point: land, power and shell (−24, before any declaration exists); network and large contracts (−15, at Intent); machines and parts (−6, at Dated); turn-up and allocation (−1, at Configured); placement and admission (launch, Live). Orange brackets mark the range still open at each commit point; at the land, power and shell commit point the whole range is still open. Instruments on the right: envelope for the portfolio and options; buy toward the high through options and cancel windows; buy to the base with the high as options, a reserve or a bridge; rank, cut line and grants; bridges and admission control. Illustrative. At each dot a tag names the stage the declaration has reached. At −15 the range still open is 40,000 to 100,000 requests per second; at −6, a base of 60,000 and a high of 90,000. A note says the bars are simplified; the method stacks need dates and uses cautious lead times.
